scope: Re-read all 12 changed Samuel persons_1 drafts against fixed WEB witness and current article-body evidence. This is a delta closure, not a replacement for the original 84-row independent review. Author drafts/evidence were not edited.
decisionPolicyJa: 元指摘は閉じたかを現稿の本文・facts/gates・出典で再確認した。qualifiedは原文の文脈推定/表記差/記事の限定性などが残る状態で、failは修正後も本文事実の誤帰属が残る状態。記事本文の実読根拠をURL/節/行で記録し、URL応答や作者metadataだけを記事確認とは扱わない。

items.previousIndependentFinding: Wiki note at knownBy 15:8 describes survival of Saul’s campaign and Samuel’s execution (later 15:33); fresh article read lines 123 and 126 confirms these are later narrative facts.
items.assessmentJa: 15:8 summary identifies Agag as Amalekite king captured alive. Later treatment at 15:9, 15:20, 15:32, 15:33 is separated into facts with corresponding knownBy gates. Wiki note now only identifies the article subject and contains no later survival/execution information.

wikipediaBodyReview.findingJa: L126 discusses the later survival and execution; current note avoids those details and states only the article concerns the Amalekite king Agag of 1 Samuel 15.

items.previousIndependentFinding: Profile passages/facts at 1SA23:6 and 30:7 describe Abiathar, Ahimelech’s son; 30:7 has Abiathar as the addressee and the one who brings the ephod. These are not actions or name occurrences of Ahimelech.
items.assessmentJa: Removed the erroneous 23:6/30:7 Abiathar actions and retained Ahimelech’s own 21:1–22:16 appearances plus the 22:20 father/son mention. The base says he welcomed David while fearing Saul; WEB 21:1 directly says he came trembling, while fear of Saul is inferred from surrounding context rather than named in that verse.

wikipediaBodyReview.findingJa: Describes the Nob priest visited by David while fleeing Saul; supports the person match.

items.previousIndependentFinding: The sole fact at 1SA6:14 says cart wood was split and cows offered; the WEB verse does not assign these actions to Joshua.
items.assessmentJa: The unsupported 6:14 action fact was removed. Summary accurately limits Joshua to owner named in the field where the cart stopped; 6:18 separately names his field. The note distinguishes this Beth-shemesh landowner from Joshua son of Nun.

items.previousIndependentFinding: At knownBy 1SA2:27, summary explicitly says Pharaoh is used again in 6:6; the verse 6:6 is later and may concern another ruler.
items.assessmentJa: 2:27 summary now only discusses the house of Pharaoh in the ancestors’ Egypt account. The profile retains a distinct 6:6 title occurrence. Since Pharaoh is an office title and the WEB does not identify a personal king, the office-title record appropriately avoids a named ruler; the note about multiple historical periods is a general title distinction, not a specific king claim.

sourceCoordinatesReviewed.text: A man of God came to Eli and said to him, “The LORD says, ‘Did I reveal myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt in bondage to Pharaoh’s house?
Why then do you harden your hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? When he had worked wonderfully among them, didn’t they let the people go, and they departed?

wikipediaBodyReview.findingJa: Defines Pharaoh as a title for ancient Egyptian kings; supports the office-title concept but does not identify the ruler(s) in Samuel.

items.previousIndependentFinding: Fixed WEB 2SA8:17 says “Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were priests.” Current base and fact makes Abiathar himself the named priest; the verse names Ahimelech son of Abiathar as priest and Abiathar as father. Fresh Wikipedia read lines 134–142 likewise identifies Abiathar as Ahimelech’s son.
items.assessmentJa: The 8:17 base now says Ahimelech is named as Abiathar’s son, not that Abiathar is the priest in that clause. Current 15:35 fact correctly records David’s instruction involving Zadok and Abiathar and includes the 15:35 passage/source. The remaining qualification is textual: the linked article’s “Confusion of the name” section explains the proposed reading “Ahimelech son of Abiathar” at 2 Samuel 8:17, while its usual account identifies Abiathar as Ahimelech’s son. The profile faithfully follows fixed WEB and relation note rather than asserting the variant away.
